html:
SMTO-EXE-0100 — The computer sent back a screen result SMTO couldn't trust

GUID: 7282b403-f10c-5db3-b77f-e765afcb7bac
Slug: screen-invalid-response
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: screen

What happened

  • The Gateway answered SMTO's screen request, but the answer was incomplete or didn't match what was asked, for example the picture was the wrong size. SMTO threw the answer away.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways, select Check for updates, and if an Update to button with a version number appears for that Gateway, use it while no task is running there. A Gateway on a different version from SMTO can send answers in a form SMTO won't accept. Updating stops that Gateway's running tasks, so wait until they finish.
  2. Don't change the screen resolution, scaling or monitor setup on that computer while SMTO is capturing. A change during the capture makes the picture's size differ from what SMTO asked for.
  3. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways, select Check connection for that Gateway, then start a New chat and ask for the screenshot again. A new chat uses the Gateway's refreshed abilities for a fresh request.

What success looks like

  • SMTO returns the screenshot or text you asked for.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send it, with the Error ID, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't paste screenshots or screen contents into the report.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Screen result validation failed: fields not allowed for the operation, contradictory success flags, an unknown error kind, undecodable or oversized worker output, or native raster dimensions that differ from the requested pixel bounds.

What this means

  • Screen receipt validation found incompatible fields, unsolicited or malformed content, incorrect native pixel-buffer dimensions or an invalid worker response. Screen and OCR observations occur only through their existing explicit request and permission flow. Rendering diagnostics neither captures pixels nor reads additional content, and no failed observation is silently repeated.

Why this can happen

  • Screen receipt validation found incompatible fields, unsolicited or malformed content, incorrect native pixel-buffer dimensions or an invalid worker response.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect structural receipt diagnostics and expected geometry without exposing screen content in error reports.

How to fix it

  • Refresh the Gateway's version and capabilities, then report the Error ID with structural diagnostics only. validate_response and native_call reject unsolicited fields, ok/executed/complete contradictions and undecodable worker output; the adapters reject X11 stride or Quartz size mismatches. Never treat incomplete or unsolicited screen content as a successful observation.
  • Refresh Gateway version/capabilities and report the Error ID with structural diagnostics. Do not treat incomplete or unsolicited screen content as successful evidence.

Retry and execution caution

  • Refresh Gateway version/capabilities and report the Error ID with structural diagnostics. Do not treat incomplete or unsolicited screen content as successful evidence.

How to verify the fix

  • The result passes its operation-specific contract and only explicitly requested content is accepted as evidence.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass OS permissions, capture another Gateway, or copy screen content to diagnostics.

Technical notes

  • Screen and OCR observations occur only through their existing explicit request and permission flow. Rendering diagnostics neither captures pixels nor reads additional content, and no failed observation is silently repeated.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
